images.title: Rectangle minus two corners
images.purpose: Shows the shaded region found by subtracting two corner triangles from an 18 cm by 10 cm rectangle.
images.composition: One rectangle, large and centred, with two white corner triangles cut off and the rest shaded.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A rectangle 18 units wide and 10 units tall, corners A top left, B top right, C bottom right, D bottom left (letters not drawn). E is on the top side 10 units from A (8 units from B). F is on the left side 6 units below A (4 units above D). Corner triangle AEF (legs 10 and 6) and corner triangle EBC (legs 8 and 10) are left white with grey (#6B7280) dashed hatch outlines. The quadrilateral FECD is filled teal (#0072B2). Labels: 18 cm above the top side; 10 cm beside the right side; 30 cm² inside triangle AEF; 40 cm² inside triangle EBC; 110 cm² inside the teal region. Check: 18 × 10 = 180, 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30, 1/2 × 8 × 10 = 40, 180 − 30 − 40 = 110.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Take the corners away from the rectangle: 180 − 30 − 40 = 110 cm².
images.description: Shows the shaded region found by subtracting two corner triangles from an 18 cm by 10 cm rectangle.
images.context: Practice concept; matches the shaded region exercise (AB = 18, BC = 10, AE = 10, AF = 6).
images.teaching_notes: Ask which is quicker here: splitting into triangles or subtracting corners.

image_decisions.why: Subtracting corners from an enclosing rectangle is a visual method the child must see once.
